what_its_for: Diltiazem is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension), chest pain (angina), and certain heart rhythm problems (such as atrial fibrillation). It works by relaxing the blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard, and it helps control your heart rate.
how_to_take: Take diltiazem exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow extended-release capsules or tablets whole — do NOT crush, chew, or break them, as this can release too much medicine at once and cause serious side effects. Some capsules (like Tiazac) can be opened and sprinkled on a spoonful of applesauce — swallow right away without chewing. Immediate-release tablets can be taken with or without food. Extended-release forms are often taken once a day; some forms are taken twice a day. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, other medications, and how well your body responds. Do NOT change your dose without talking to your doctor first. Common starting doses vary widely depending on which form you take. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions on your prescription label.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — UNLESS it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take the next one at your regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store diltiazem at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking diltiazem, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood to unsafe levels. Avoid alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and increase dizziness. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how diltiazem affects you, since it may cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Avoid getting up too quickly from a sitting or lying position to reduce the risk of falls. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about ALL medications you take, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, as many medicines interact with diltiazem.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: a very slow or irregular heartbeat, chest pain that gets worse, fainting or severe dizziness, swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles, shortness of breath, yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems), unusual bruising or bleeding, or a skin rash. Also call your doctor if your blood pressure readings are unusually high or low, or if you feel your condition is not improving.
when_it_works: For high blood pressure and chest pain, you may start to feel better within a few days, but it can take 1 to 2 weeks to see the full benefit. For heart rhythm problems, your doctor will monitor your response closely. Keep taking diltiazem even if you feel well — high blood pressure often has no symptoms, and stopping suddenly can be dangerous. Do NOT stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Talk to your doctor before taking diltiazem if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It is generally not recommended during pregnancy. BREASTFEEDING: Diltiazem passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. OLDER ADULTS: Older patients may be more sensitive to the effects of diltiazem (such as dizziness and low blood pressure) and may need a lower dose. Rise slowly from sitting or lying down to avoid falls. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor may need to adjust your dose, as the medicine can build up in your body. Always tell your doctor about all your health conditions before starting this medication.
